newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natural gas climbs on cold weather.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natural gas climbs on cold weather.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices jumped in busy trade again on Wednesday as cold weather in Alberta caused problems with some gas plants and utilities maintained their demand, traders said.

Gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub was quoted as high as C$1.90 per gigajoule, up from C$1.57 per GJ last week and C$1.67 on Tuesday. December AECO gas fetched about C$1.88 per GJ, up from C$1.575 the week before.
"Some of the plants in the province had some electrical problems because of the dense fog," said a Calgary-based marketer. Alberta has had ice fog and snow over the past week.
"Also, utilities have been buying day gas and there is not much withdrawal (of gas from storage)," he said.
Traders said prices were expected to climb higher by the weekend, with temperatures in southern Alberta forecast to dip to a frosty low of minus-25 Celsius (-13 Fahrenheit) Sunday.
At the borders, prices at Sumas, Washington fell by 15 cents on the week to trade in the US$2.10/2.15 range, as warmer weather on the U.S. West Coast eased demand.

Gas at Niagara, Ontario climbed about 17 cents from November 6 to trade at about US$3.17 per mmBtu. Less storage volume was being withdrawn this week than in the U.S. Midwest and Northeast where prices softened, marketers said. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
